name: pidfd_send_signal
synopsis: int syscall(SYS_pidfd_send_signal, int pidfd, int sig, siginfo_t *_Nullable info, unsigned int flags);
description: The pidfd_send_signal() system call sends a signal to a process identified by a PID file descriptor. It allows specifying additional signal information via a siginfo_t structure if provided. The caller must be in the appropriate PID namespace, and flags must be set to 0.

parameters.name: pidfd
parameters.description: File descriptor referring to the target process

parameters.name: info
parameters.description: Pointer to a siginfo_t structure for additional information, or NULL for default values

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Reserved for future use; must be set to 0

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: pidfd is not a valid PID file descriptor
sig is not a valid signal
The calling process is not in a PID namespace from which it can send a signal to the target process
The calling process does not have permission to send the signal to the target process
pidfd doesn’t refer to the calling process, and info.si_code is invalid
The target process does not exist

examples: static int pidfd_send_signal(int pidfd, int sig, siginfo_t *info, unsigned int flags) { return syscall(SYS_pidfd_send_signal, pidfd, sig, info, flags); }
